items.headline: AI's financing boom is hitting its first constraint: investor capacity
items.teaser: AI infrastructure is increasingly being paid for with debt, and bond investors are starting to ask for more yield. The story is moving from capex to capital markets — which changes how fast ROI has to show up.
items.body: U.S. technology companies are financing AI infrastructure with debt at a scale that changed inside a year: AI-related corporate bond issuance is running at roughly $220 billion in 2026 against about $12.5 billion in 2025, and investors are beginning to demand higher yields as their exposure grows — even from highly rated issuers. That turns AI from a software and capex story into a capital-markets story, and it moves the pressure to prove return on enormous data-centre investment out of the pitch deck and into operations. For anyone whose work lowers the cost of running that infrastructure — energy optimisation, cooling, capacity planning, hardware utilisation, data-centre operations — the value of that work goes up from here.
